nonblocking_deferrals: ICS source/revision and source-dependent idle-expiry recovery questions are DEFERRED_NONBLOCKING per user; no re-investigation or owner question.

claim_checks.claim: Activity-based continued renewal, now bounded by idle <=15 min and absolute <=60 min; manual recovery and initial refresh-credential boundary remain within absolute deadline
claim_checks.confidence: high for activity categories and timeout ceilings; medium for inherited detailed prompt transitions
claim_checks.rationale: Exact user input supplies activity categories, continuing renewal, ownership and ceilings. Earlier unbounded elapsed-time intent is explicitly superseded. Detailed prompt criteria are inherited from the accepted correction, whose retained source is terse; no contradictory current answer was found.
limits: Exact token lifetimes and configured renewal interval remain unspecified.
No current runtime conformance or publication approval is established.

claim_checks.claim: AC YAML and body Gherkin agree
claim_checks.rationale: All nine structured criteria match their Gherkin counterparts; the same unsupported timing condition is repeated in AC-1 to AC-3.

findings.evidence: All five registered sources were read in full. They specify eligible activity and continued renewal but no 100 ms event cadence, 15 s completion window, or 30 s starting horizon. Predecessor v7 at git 79395ced1 contains the same timing values, which proves inheritance only.
findings.consequence: A conforming implementation whose configured renewal point falls outside the arbitrary 15 s window can fail the canonical requirement. The Given does not establish that renewal is due.
findings.next_action: Root to correct only AC-1 to AC-3 in structured fields and body; leave historical executions unchanged.

proposed_correction.given: Given a valid portal session at its configured renewal-due point before both access expiry and absolute session expiry
proposed_correction.when: When eligible mouse movement, keyboard input, or scrolling continues (one activity type per criterion)
proposed_correction.then: Then at least one renewal succeeds before the current access deadline and before the absolute session deadline

findings.resolution: Resolved by root v9 correction and independent final-byte recheck; original v8 finding retained.

final_byte_recheck.source_bindings: Same five registered sources as the v8 review; unchanged source tuples and verified snapshot hashes.
checks: AC-1 to AC-3 now require eligible activity when renewal is due and success before existing access and absolute deadlines.
No arbitrary event frequency, 15-second completion window, 30-second starting horizon or new token lifetime remains.
All nine structured criteria match their body Gherkin steps.
AC-4 to AC-9 remain byte-equivalent as structured values to the assigned v8 baseline.
Predecessor fields bind v9 to the reviewed v8 hash.
limits: No formal human ASD-STE100/content/publication approval is inferred.
No runtime behavior or deployment conformance was verified.
ICS source and source-dependent idle-recovery review remain deferred nonblocking.

claim_checks.rationale: 15-minute access/24-hour refresh examples, <60/<15 strict wording, 105 versus225 refresh contradiction, auth_time changes and no-absolute claim are attributed and qualified rather than accepted as current policy.

claim_checks.claim: Historical Entra onboarding/profile differences and FMAA account validity
claim_checks.rationale: Pilot scope, profile differences, one-hour provider session and exceptional FMAA durations remain source statements. None establishes current portal token policy or deployed conformance.

claim_checks.rationale: All Gherkin counts reflect the explicit decision. Multiple-entity matching and data permissions are not inferred. Conflicting historical allow-SC/empty-role examples remain qualified and distinct from empty entity.

claim_checks.claim: Tile validation on login, reload, idle extension and next-login UI revocation
claim_checks.rationale: Validation criterion applies available entitlement data and does not invent its freshness. UI revocation is tested at next login, with pre-login tab behavior left unresolved.

claim_checks.rationale: Scenario is explicitly conditional on the API using the cache being tested. No combined deadline, JWT lifetime or cache-interaction order is invented.

claim_checks.claim: SDK authentication, request context, EMS2 permissions and application enforcement boundary
claim_checks.rationale: Filter authentication, exclusion ordering, skip-header uncertainty, two entitlement retrieval modes and token separation match the guides. Visible tile and entitlement retrieval are not equated with data/action enforcement.

claim_checks.claim: Version/configuration and Boot4 history
claim_checks.rationale: Artifacts, platforms, renamed fields, max_age/oud, logout blacklist notes and Boot4 snapshot condition match exact source. Present deployments and compatibility remain unverified.

claim_checks.claim: Existing frontend caller API compatibility and independent per-tile admission
claim_checks.rationale: Cases preserve existing calls within reviewed mappings and separate role multiplicity. Two tiles define a case population only. EMS3 is explicitly recorded interpretation of the source wording; not a silent change to quotation.

claim_checks.rationale: Zero writes/fabricated scalar owners implements the explicit pending decision. Query visibility and role-exclusion policy remain unresolved, avoiding invented follow-on rules.

claim_checks.rationale: Boolean union cases match either-provider acceptance; no new caller scope required. Logging accepted grant source matches user request; per-tile admission and scalar role issues remain separate.

claim_checks.rationale: Entitlement names remain application scoped. name RATAN_ENTITLEMENT_RULE, team label RATAN and applicationId 51358 are distinct; no arbitrary scalar role or cross-application label is invented. Existing fields and EMS2 behavior remain within the compatibility objective.

claim_checks.claim: Evidence limits and unresolved data restrictions, CES-only scope, scalar role and complete API mappings
claim_checks.rationale: The record explicitly separates expectations from execution, target metadata from deployed contracts, and unresolved role semantics from known mapped permissions. Open decisions do not block completing the bounded candidate semantic review.
